title: A Meta-Research Review of Statistical Practices for Image-Reliant AI Tools Predicting Lung Cancer Outcomes
zh_title: 肺癌影像AI统计方法学的元研究综述
summary: 对2023至2025年36项肺癌影像AI研究进行元研究综述，评估其统计方法与报告规范。
key_points: 纳入36项肺癌影像AI研究
75%使用卷积神经网络
81%以AUC为主要评价指标
reason: 纳入36项研究的同行评审元研究综述，方法学信息有价值，但非临床验证，属值得一看档。
abstract: AbstractAI models using medical images are increasingly proposed to support clinical decision-making in lung cancer, motivating assessment of their methodological rigor and transparency. To assess how these models are developed, evaluated, and reported, and to identify gaps in best statistical practices, we conducted a cross-sectional meta-research review of OpenAlex-indexed studies (January 1, 2023, to June 30, 2025) that developed image-based AI tools for lung cancer risk prediction, detection, or prognosis. Thirty-six studies met our inclusion criteria. Convolutional neural networks were used in most studies (27 studies, 75%), and area under the curve (AUC) was the most frequently reported evaluation metric (29 studies, 81%). Although 23 studies (64%) reported some form of uncertainty quantification, most were limited to presenting confidence intervals for global performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, and accuracy) rather than individual prediction- or risk-level uncertainty. Common limitations included limited external test set use (14 studies, 39%), insufficient subgroup analyses (10 studies, 28%), and limited adherence to established prediction-model reporting guidelines. Overall, future research should prioritize standardized reporting, use of external test sets, and model performance assessment across clinically relevant subpopulations. The coexistence of increasingly powerful AI-based prediction models with inconsistent study design, evaluation, and reporting practices emphasizes the urgent need to implement more rigorous and transparent methodological standards in this field. (Funded by Yale School of Public Health.).
zh_abstract: 摘要：使用医学图像的AI（人工智能）模型正越来越多地被提出用于支持肺癌的临床决策，这促使人们评估其方法学严谨性和透明度。为评估这些模型如何被开发、评估和报告，并识别最佳统计实践方面的差距，我们对OpenAlex索引的研究（2023年1月1日至2025年6月30日）进行了一项横断面元研究综述，这些研究开发了基于图像的AI工具用于肺癌风险预测、检测或预后。36项研究符合我们的纳入标准。大多数研究使用了卷积神经网络（convolutional neural networks）（27项研究，75%），曲线下面积（AUC）是最常报告的评估指标（29项研究，81%）。尽管23项研究（64%）报告了某种形式的不确定性量化，但大多数仅限于呈现全局性能指标（如AUC、敏感性和准确性）的置信区间，而非个体预测层面或风险层面的不确定性。常见局限性包括外部测试集使用有限（14项研究，39%）、亚组分析不足（10项研究，28%），以及对既定预测模型报告指南的依从性有限。总体而言，未来研究应优先考虑标准化报告、使用外部测试集，以及在临床相关亚人群中评估模型性能。日益强大的基于AI的预测模型与不一致的研究设计、评估和报告实践并存，强调该领域迫切需要实施更严谨和透明的方法学标准。（由耶鲁大学公共卫生学院资助。）

abstract: The European Medical Device Regulations have been criticized for imposing disproportionate barriers to innovation due to excessive regulatory requirements. In response, the European Commission proposed amendments to key regulations in December 2025. The reforms aim to eliminate double regulation, reduce documentation requirements, and introduce new regulatory tools. In this Comment, we argue that these changes are generally well-targeted but leave specific challenges for innovative artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices unresolved.
zh_abstract: 欧盟医疗器械法规（European Medical Device Regulations）因过度监管要求对创新造成不成比例的障碍而受到批评。作为回应，欧盟委员会（European Commission）于2025年12月提出对关键法规的修订。改革旨在消除双重监管、减少文件要求，并引入新的监管工具。在本评论（Comment）中，我们认为这些变化总体目标明确，但仍未解决创新性人工智能赋能医疗器械所面临的具体挑战。

title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
zh_title: TabBioMed：大规模生物医学表格学习基准
summary: arXiv 预印本发布 94 个公开生物医学表格数据集基准，统一预处理与评测框架，并对比 23 个模型。
key_points: 含 94 个公开生物医学表格数据集
覆盖电子病历、药物发现与多类组学
23 个模型中表格基础模型族表现最佳
reason: 94 数据集、23 模型的大型公开基准；但为预印本，属重要档
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have accelerated biomedical prediction, but evaluation on structured biomedical data remains fragmented, especially for datasets with high dimensionality, large sample size, missingness, and class imbalance. We introduce TabBioMed, a large-scale benchmark of 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets spanning electronic health records, drug discovery, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, and systems biology. TabBioMed unifies these datasets through a standardized, dataset-aware preprocessing and evaluation framework, enabling reproducible comparison across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks. We benchmark 23 models across classical baselines, gradient-boosted trees, neural tabular architectures, and tabular foundation models. Foundation models deliver the strongest family-level predictive performance. However, their gains are regime-dependent: tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain highly competitive, often dominating under inference-time or training-cost constraints. Overall, TabBioMed shows that biomedical tabular learning is strongly context-dependent, with optimal model choice depending on data regime, task type, and computational budget. We release TabBioMed with curated datasets and splits, preprocessing code, baselines, and results, providing a reproducible benchmark for practical model selection and future methods development in biomedical machine learning, available at https://github.com/AI-sandbox/TabBioMed.
zh_abstract: 机器学习的最新进展加速了生物医学预测，但在结构化生物医学数据上的评估仍然碎片化，尤其是对于具有高维、大样本量、缺失和类别不平衡的数据集。我们推出TabBioMed，一个大规模基准，包含94个经过整理的公开生物医学表格数据集，涵盖电子健康记录、药物发现、基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学、单细胞组学和系统生物学。TabBioMed通过标准化、感知数据集的预处理和评估框架统一这些数据集，从而能够在分类、回归和多目标任务之间进行可复现比较。我们对23个模型进行了基准测试，涵盖经典基线、梯度提升树、神经表格架构和表格基础模型。基础模型在家族层面提供了最强的预测性能。然而，它们的增益依赖于数据情形（regime）：基于树的模型和调优的多层感知机仍极具竞争力，在推理时间或训练成本约束下常常占优。总体而言，TabBioMed表明生物医学表格学习强烈依赖情境，最佳模型选择取决于数据情形、任务类型和计算预算。我们发布TabBioMed，包含整理后的数据集和划分、预处理代码、基线和结果，为生物医学机器学习中的实际模型选择和未来方法开发提供可复现的基准，网址为 https://github.com/AI-sandbox/TabBioMed。

title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
zh_title: InclusionMed：面向包容性医疗的AI评测基准
summary: 预印本提出开放医疗AI评测计划 InclusionMed，从388个候选中筛出4个公开基准，加自建诊断推理基准共5项，前沿大模型综合得分17.5–49.1。
key_points: Atlas按3种医疗角色×3种能力组织
首版覆盖9格中的3格
reason: 预印本新公开评测基准但覆盖不完整，属值得一看档
abstract: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index, with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered. A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost. These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection. Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.
zh_abstract: 推动面向包容性医疗的医学AI需要跨多样医疗角色、任务和照护场景的评估，但基准覆盖仍不均衡。我们推出InclusionMed，一项面向包容性医疗的开放式医学AI评估倡议。InclusionMed Atlas将基准按三个医疗角色和三种AI能力组织。首个版本中，我们通过结构化审查和独立复现，从388个候选基准中选出了四个公开基准。加上我们的私有诊断推理基准InclusionMed-DxFiles，Atlas共包含五个基准，覆盖其九个角色—能力单元中的三个。我们在Atlas上评估了前沿大语言模型，并将结果汇总为InclusionMed Index，总体得分范围为17.5至49.1（满分100）。该Index还按医疗角色和AI能力报告得分，显示模型的排名会随所考虑的角色或能力而变化。使用任务级标签的基准内分析显示，Index中排名最高的十个模型在患者沟通上的得分均高于临床决策。Index得分相近的模型在估计推理成本上也存在显著差异。这些发现凸显了需要覆盖更多样化医疗需求的评估，以及针对具体情境选择模型。通过开放合作和社区贡献，InclusionMed力求确保全球多样化的医疗需求能够塑造医学AI进展的定义和衡量方式。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University; conditions: Postoperative Pulmonary Complications (PPCs); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 1500; status: ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION] Background and Objective Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after elective colorectal surgery and are associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and delayed recovery. Existing PPC prediction tools were mainly developed in thoracic or mixed surgical populations and rely predominantly on clinical variables; preoperative chest CT information remains underused, and a population-specific tool for elderly colorectal cancer patients is still lacking. This study aims to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning model that integrates preoperative chest CT-derived features with multidimensional clinical variables to predict PPCs in patients aged ≥65 years undergoing elective radical colorectal cancer surgery, and to quantify its incremental value and clinical net benefit. Methods This is a single-center retrospective cohort study. Eligible patients will be assigned to a development window (August 2020-August 2024), split chronologically at a 7∶1∶2 ratio into training, validation, and test sets with five-fold cross-validation, and a locked temporal external validation window (September 2024-September 2026), which will be used only after the final model is fixed. The primary outcome is 30-day composite PPCs defined according to the EPCO criteria; the Melbourne Group Scale will serve as a parallel sensitivity definition. Preoperative clinical variables and chest CT images obtained within four weeks before surgery will be collected. A convolutional neural network imaging branch-or 2D transfer learning based on RadImageNet if the sample size is insufficient-will extract CT deep features, which will be fused with clinical variables at the feature (intermediate) level. Six classifiers, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron, will be tuned within a unified search space. Discrimination (AUC with DeLong test and Bootstrap 95% CI), calibration (calibration curves, Brier score), incremental value (NRI, IDI), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis) will be evaluated against the ARISCAT and GSU-Pulmonary scores, a clinical-only model, and an imaging-only model. Grad-CAM and SHAP will be applied to interpret the model. Expected Outcome The study is expected to provide an interpretable and deployable preoperative risk stratification tool for elderly patients undergoing colorectal surgery, clarify the incremental contribution of preoperative chest CT inf
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：宁夏医科大学总医院（General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University）；疾病：术后肺部并发症（Postoperative Pulmonary Complications, PPCs）；类型：OBSERVATIONAL；入组人数：1500；状态：ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION] 【背景与目的】术后肺部并发症（PPCs）在择期结直肠手术后常见，并与住院时间延长、发病率增加和恢复延迟相关。现有的PPC预测工具主要在胸科或混合手术人群中开发，且主要依赖临床变量；术前胸部CT信息仍未得到充分利用，且仍缺乏针对老年结直肠癌患者的人群特异性工具。本研究旨在开发并验证一种多模态深度学习模型，该模型整合术前胸部CT衍生特征与多维临床变量，用于预测年龄≥65岁接受择期结直肠癌根治术患者的PPCs，并量化其增量价值和临床净获益。 【方法】这是一项单中心回顾性队列研究。符合条件的患者将被分配至开发窗口（2020年8月至2024年8月），按时间顺序以7∶1∶2的比例分为训练集、验证集和测试集，并进行五折交叉验证；同时设置锁定的时间外部验证窗口（2024年9月至2026年9月），仅在最终模型固定后使用。主要结局是根据EPCO标准定义的30天复合PPCs；墨尔本小组量表（Melbourne Group Scale）将作为平行的敏感性定义。将收集术前临床变量和手术前四周内获得的胸部CT图像。将使用卷积神经网络影像分支——若样本量不足，则使用基于RadImageNet的二维迁移学习——提取CT深度特征，并在特征（中间）层面与临床变量融合。六种分类器，包括逻辑回归、支持向量机、随机森林、XGBoost、LightGBM和多层感知机，将在统一搜索空间内调参。将针对ARISCAT和GSU-Pulmonary评分、仅临床模型和仅影像模型评估区分度（AUC，采用DeLong检验和Bootstrap 95% CI）、校准度（校准曲线、Brier评分）、增量价值（NRI、IDI）和临床效用（决策曲线分析）。将应用Grad-CAM和SHAP解释模型。 【预期结局】本研究预期为接受结直肠手术的老年患者提供一种可解释且可部署的术前风险分层工具，阐明术前胸部CT inf的增量贡献。

title: Machine Learning Approaches to Biologic Therapy Response in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Review Article.
zh_title: 机器学习预测IBD生物制剂应答综述

abstract: [Sage open pathology] Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, remains a complex and heterogeneous condition with variable response to biologic therapies. Despite significant advances with anti-TNF agents, integrin inhibitors, and interleukin-12/23 blockers, treatment outcomes are limited by primary nonresponse, secondary loss of efficacy, immunogenicity, and substantial healthcare costs. The advent of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms, offers new opportunities to address these challenges by integrating diverse clinical, laboratory, imaging, histologic, genetic, and microbiome data. Recent studies demonstrate that AI-based models achieve high accuracy in predicting biologic response, remission, and adverse outcomes, outperforming conventional statistical approaches. AI has also shown promise in real-time endoscopic assessment, histologic grading, and forecasting disease progression, enabling earlier intervention and personalized therapy. However, current models are constrained by limited datasets, heterogeneity, lack of large-scale prospective validation, and concerns regarding interpretability, transparency, and patient privacy. Future efforts should prioritize multicenter trials, external validation, and ethical integration into clinical workflows. Collectively, AI-driven prediction of biologic therapy response represents a pivotal step toward precision medicine in IBD, with the potential to optimize therapeutic strategies, reduce ineffective treatment exposure, and improve patient outcomes.
zh_abstract: [Sage open pathology] 炎症性肠病（inflammatory bowel disease, IBD），包括克罗恩病（Crohn's disease）和溃疡性结肠炎（ulcerative colitis），仍然是一种复杂且异质性的疾病，对生物制剂的反应存在差异。尽管抗TNF药物、整合素抑制剂和白细胞介素-12/23阻断剂取得了显著进展，但治疗结局仍受原发性无应答、继发性疗效丧失、免疫原性和巨大医疗成本的限制。人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI），特别是机器学习（machine learning, ML）和深度学习（deep learning, DL）算法的出现，通过整合多样化的临床、实验室、影像、组织学、遗传和微生物组数据，为解决这些挑战提供了新机会。近期研究表明，基于AI的模型在预测生物制剂反应、缓解和不良结局方面达到较高准确度，优于传统统计方法。AI在实时内镜评估、组织学分级和预测疾病进展方面也显示出前景，可实现更早干预和个体化治疗。然而，当前模型受限于数据集有限、异质性、缺乏大规模前瞻性验证，以及对可解释性、透明性和患者隐私的担忧。未来工作应优先开展多中心试验、外部验证，并将伦理整合到临床工作流程中。总体而言，AI驱动的生物治疗反应预测是迈向IBD精准医学的关键一步，具有优化治疗策略、减少无效治疗暴露和改善患者结局的潜力。
